claim: MIT researchers reported flexible charged ligands controlling nanoparticle lattice connectivity.
verifiedFacts: MIT published a November 2 account of a Nature Materials study on flexible charged ligand-mediated nanoparticle assembly.
Researchers reported tuning connections by particle size and ligand chain length and producing previously unseen crystal structures.
The reported findings are laboratory materials research, not industrial photonics deployment.
inference: Scientific mechanism visualization could explain structural parameters while preserving evidence and attribution boundaries.
Shader Grammar must not conflate nanoparticle lattice assembly with browser optical appearance.
The result refines material-mechanism ontology but does not justify a new product.
Advisory disposition: REFERENCE-ONLY Shader Grammar/Gallery; INCUBATE Omni-Loom.
significance: The study provides a physical example of parameter-dependent self-assembly suitable for carefully bounded visual teaching.
assumptions: The experimental mechanism generalizes beyond the studied conditions.
knownLimitations: Full Nature Materials methods and raw measurements not independently inspected; scale-up and material performance unknown.
